Album.thoughts: Very alright album, the synths are immaculate. Some songs are very gloopy and nostalgic in parts. It really reminds me of minecraft and some sort of pixar music. However, it is very much like clubby. Not my favorite album, but it still sounds fairly pretty. There is nothing wrong with the album, but nothing that really stands out either.

Album.albumName: She Reaches Out To She Reaches Out To She

Album.thoughts: All around fairly good punk album, especially considering I have a bias against british punk. This band is apparently very influential, and you can hear it. The similarities to so many other punk bands is crazy. If this was made modern day I'd say it would be a 5, but since it was made in the fucking 70s, 7.5. (I just hate british people)

Very unique album, not my type of music, but it still is really solid. It tells a story in a chaotic, yet interesting, way. I dislike the first few songs where it sounds like Alastor from Hazbin Hotel is singing, but the instrumentals are very very nice. I think overall the album is fine, very folk-punky with the standout track being Grendel's Mother. Such a pretty track.

An emotionally pretty album, very egyptian in the best way possible. It flows well, it feels lively, the vocals are stellar, and it simply feels, in lack of a better term, woody, I am talking the dusty "oh this dry forest has an old stick here" type of feel. It is simple, and doesn't need more.

Not usually a fan of hip-hop, but this album is so pretty. The lyricism is so fucking good, the commentary is great and its just such a great album. I was blown away with how good it is, and I can see myself coming back to it in the future.

Album.albumName: A Walk Through The Ambient Garden

Album.thoughts: This album is raw, emotional, and intense. The sound of this whole album is softly romantic with its yearning and passonate lustful feel. I almost cried at how stunning this album is, and I lack the words to properly express what I feel about this album.

Album.albumName: Box for Buddy, Box for Star

Album.thoughts: A beautiful folk/country album, and I do not usually like country music. Super somber, romantic, and hopeful. It is very calming overall and the vocals are amazing, their voice gives me head the entire album. The guitar as well, it's really pleasant. It feels like a full story as well, and a rollercoaster.

Such a stunning album, the way the instruments drown out the vocals in this happy, yet melancholy, way. At times in the album it feels almost initmate with how they overlap and the complexities of the instrumentals. It is one of the best albums I have ever heard.

Album.albumName: Geometry of Murder: Extra Capsular Extraction Inversions
The Past Is a Garden I Never Fed
Album.thoughts: I think this album sounds like goth music if it was more upbeat and happy, yet still somber and depressing. I fear the best way I can discribe the albums is that it felt like listening to disintegration for the first time again. Poeticlly beautiful lyrics with deep somber instrumentals, truly a great album.

Album.albumName: No More Stories Are Told Today...

Album.thoughts: I Love My Mom is such a pretty, depressing, and hopeful album all at once; It's a personification of romanticized sadness and longing. It is a really good indie rock album, and an extremely stunning one at that.

Album.albumName: The Court Of The Crimson King
Everything That Dies Someday Comes Back
Album.thoughts: It is some really good metal, will give more later.

Such a visceral album in its sound and instrumentals. The way it throws emotions of discomfort and stress around, in an artificial, yet insanely human, way. Yet the vocals really such, so does the flow of the album.

Album.albumName: An Undying Love For A Burning World
The Higher the Hair, the Closer to God
By the Time I Get to Phoenix
I Know A Girl Who Develops Crime Scene Photos
Public Castration Is A Good Idea
